newsitem.title: CANADA: Prudential sells Canadian real estate to Oxford, GE.
newsitem.headline: Prudential sells Canadian real estate to Oxford, GE.

text.p: The Prudential Insurance Company of America said Monday it agreed to sell its Canadian real estate portfolio for $455.8 million to a 50/50 joint venture of Oxford Properties Group Inc. and GE Capital Canada Inc.
The sale includes five Toronto land parcels and 43 commercial properties from coast to coast with about 5.6 million square feet of rentable area.
The deadline for bids was July 16 and the deal is scheduled to close in mid-September, subject to regulatory approvals.
Prudential is the largest life insurance company in North America and one of the most diversified financial institutions in the world, with assets of $182.7 billion under management.
Oxford is an established commercial real estate ownership and management company.
GE Capital Canada Inc. is part of GE Capital Services, Inc., a global, diversified financial services company owned by General Electric Co.
